decisions.mark: states that MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY is the gate, and that it is commented out in the shipped mbedtls_config.h
concludes that in a DEFAULT build there is no indirection at all — mbedtls_calloc and mbedtls_free are preprocessor macros expanding directly to calloc and free
distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
states that on the macro path mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free does not exist at all — it is neither declared nor compiled, rather than being present and ignored
identifies that the pointers' defaults FAIL rather than fall back — an uninitialised calloc returns NULL and an uninitialised free does nothing
identifies the buffer allocator (MBEDTLS_MEMORY_BUFFER_ALLOC_C) as the only in-tree user of the runtime setter, installing itself over the pointers from its init function
states that the buffer allocator installs a MUTEXED pair when MBEDTLS_THREADING_C is on and a plain pair otherwise, chosen at compile time inside its init function
states that the buffer allocator itself requires MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY, so enabling it alone is not enough to route the library's allocations through it
the files that participate in choosing what mbedtls_calloc resolves to — include/mbedtls/platform.h
the files that participate in choosing what mbedtls_calloc resolves to — library/platform.c
the files that participate in choosing what mbedtls_calloc resolves to — library/memory_buffer_alloc.c
